set.body:
Raised by independent review of the Epic 3 whitener rename.

R/extractor.R passes legacy_supplied = !missing(whiten) into .resolve_observation_whitener(). missing() is FALSE whenever the argument appears in the call, including when it is explicitly NULL, so the deprecation branch fires and warns even though no whitener was supplied.

Reproduced:

  lm_extractor(X, C, whiten = NULL)                                  -> warns
  do.call(lm_extractor, list(design=X, effects=C, whiten=NULL))      -> warns

Both then correctly fall through to the identity whitener, so the result is right; only the warning is wrong.

Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

Programmatic callers routinely forward an optional argument that may be NULL (whiten = user_value_or_NULL, or a do.call with a complete argument list). Under Config/testthat/edition: 3 an unexpected warning fails the calling test, so this will surface as spurious downstream failures rather than as a visible deprecation notice.

Fix

  legacy_supplied = !missing(whiten) && !is.null(whiten)

and keep the both-supplied error keyed on !is.null(whiten) too, so that observation_whitener = L, whiten = NULL is accepted rather than rejected.

Verified correct in the same pass, no action needed
- Identity vs explicit-diag(n) vs two distinct AR whiteners all produce DIFFERENT diagnostics$observation_whitener signatures, including identity vs a numerically-equal explicit diag(n). Equal values are correctly not treated as equal identity.
- observation_whitener and the deprecated whiten produce bitwise-identical maps (max|diff| = 0).
- GLS agrees with C %*% qr.coef(qr(L %*% X), L %*% Y) to 1.5e-16; OLS to 8.3e-17.
- The identity path skips materialising diag(n) and still matches the explicit diag(n) map exactly (max|diff| = 0).
- Positional compatibility preserved: observation_whitener occupies the old third position.
set.title: lm_extractor warns spuriously when whiten = NULL is passed explicitly
